audit: docker-cp package-dir bug silent-zero audit -- broader blast radius (extends EnterpriseBench-hktt)
fingerprint: topo_order checkpoint: score==0.0 AND exit_code==1 => docker_cp_silent_zero (ModuleNotFoundError swallowed). score==0.0 AND exit_code==0 => genuine_guard_zero (real agent miss, not the bug). Identical to hktt's fingerprint; this audit reapplies it outside the two rescore_* dirs hktt scanned.
locations_scanned: results/runs/ (main checkout -- the LIVE source for aggregate_mcp_clean.py's 'locked N=105' set and, via rglob, scripts/analyze_scores.py's score_analysis.json)
results/rescore_aq8e/, results/rescore_uu17/ (hktt's original scope -- rescanned for consistency)

results_runs_findings.note: 17 distinct docker_cp_silent_zero result files under results/runs/, spanning 8 of the 11 refactor-orchestration-family tasks. 16 are read live by aggregate_mcp_clean.py (task_dir/<mode>/results.json) and therefore feed recompute_headline_aq8e.py's 'old_locked' headline directly. The 17th is a March pre-mode-split flat file for refactor-orch-003 that aggregate_mcp_clean.py ignores (it only reads the mode-subdir form) -- but that same flat file IS consumed by scripts/analyze_scores.py (rglob('results.json')), whose dedup keeps the higher normalized_score rather than the newer file, so the buggy March score (0.6) currently wins over the corrected June rerun (0.5) in the live results/score_analysis.json (verified: per_task[92] for refactor-orch-003 shows baseline=0.6). This is a second, independent defect in analyze_scores.py's dedup rule, not the docker-cp bug itself, but it means the docker-cp contamination reaches score_analysis.json -- the file the paper cites for headline numbers -- through a path hktt's audit never considered.

affected_cell_dead_for_amc_but_live_for_.note: flat legacy file (2026-03-31); superseded on disk by results/runs/refactor-orch-003/baseline/results.json (2026-06-04, genuine_guard_zero, score 0.5) but analyze_scores.py's rglob+highest-score dedup still selects this stale 0.6 file

unrelated_anomaly.note: different failure signature (exit 127 = command-not-found, not ModuleNotFoundError) -- NOT the docker-cp bug. Out of scope for this audit; worth its own investigation.

rescore_aq8e_uu17_findings.note: Rescanned hktt's original scope for consistency. Result: unchanged, exactly the same 5 instances hktt found.

rerun_9awn_findings.note: The bead described only refactor-orch-{001,007} as affected here; direct rescan of all 6 present baseline-arm result files finds 5 affected (001,002,003,004,007) and only 1 clean (008). This baseline arm is read live and UNCONDITIONALLY TRUSTED by recompute_headline_aq8e.py's rerun_baseline dict whenever phase=='complete' and success==True -- it does not check checkpoint exit_code, so all 5 buggy task_scores currently flow uncorrected into the 'uu17_mixed' headline (the accepted/closed recompute).

genuine_guard_zero_cells.note: the only clean cell among the 6 rerun_9awn baseline-arm files scanned

rerun_pt0n_findings.note: pt0n is the in-progress post-fix rerun. Currently covers only 3 cells, all baseline mode, all now genuine_guard_zero (exit_code=0) -- confirms the 07-04 fix resolves the ModuleNotFoundError. IMPORTANT SCOPE GAP: pt0n's 3 cells (001/004/007 baseline) do not fully overlap hktt's original 5 (which were aq8e/004+007 baseline AND uu17/001+007+008 mcp_only) -- it misses all 3 uu17 mcp_only cells entirely, and covers none of the 16 newly-found results/runs/ cells or the 5 newly-found rerun_9awn cells.
rerun_pt0n_findings.caveat: post-fix topo_order is STILL 0.0 for all 3 -- the fix stops the infra crash but does not by itself recover a nonzero score; each cell needs the agent's REFACTOR_PLAN.md to actually be present/valid for topo_order to score >0.
